script.title: Ways to center a card, ranked

tierlist.criterion: centered both ways, any screen size

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Let's rank the ways to center a card on a portfolio page. One rule: centered horizontally and vertically, on any screen size.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: The old center tag. It's deprecated, and it only centers horizontally. F tier.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: text-align center. It centers the text inside the card, not the card itself. D tier.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: margin auto with a fixed width. Great horizontally, but in normal flow it does nothing vertically. C tier.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Absolute position, top and left fifty percent, then translate minus fifty percent. It works everywhere. So is it S tier?

pause.prompt: position: absolute + top/left 50% + translate(-50%, -50%). Where does it rank for centering a card?
choices: B: works, but pulls the card out of the layout

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: B tier. It centers perfectly, but the card leaves the normal layout, so nothing else can flow around it.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Grid with place-items center. Two lines on the parent, centered both ways. S tier.

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Flexbox with justify-content and align-items center. Same result, works everywhere. Also S.

script.takeaway: Use flexbox or grid on the parent to center both ways; margin auto only centers horizontally.

questions.prompt: Why is text-align: center only D tier?
choices: It centers the text inside the card, not the card
questions.explanation: text-align affects inline content inside an element, not the element's own position.
